title: Deviation: Directive-4.9 and MisraC2012-20.7 for the function-like GEN_STRIP parenthesis-stripping macro (application general.h)

standards_mappings.reference: Rule/directive Directive-4.9 as written in the source annotation; normative rule text is proprietary and is not reproduced or verified by this corpus.
standards_mappings.rationale: The rule number is reproduced exactly as written in the in-source Axivion annotation at commit 308028fb. The severity classification and the normative wording of the rule are proprietary and are deliberately not asserted here.

standards_mappings.reference: SWE.4 Software Verification (static analysis evidence and justified deviance)
standards_mappings.rationale: The record is the in-source static-analysis deviance evidence for one rule set, which is part of what SWE.4 expects a project to hold. It is only partial: the repository holds no deviance log, no approval trail, no tool criticality entry for the analysing tool, and no re-analysis trigger register, so the surrounding SWE.4 evidence a qualified project would need is not evidenced at this commit.

standards_mappings.rationale: The project states a MUST for MISRA C:2012 compatibility (docs/developer-manual/software/software-programming-language.rst:22), so these suppressions are deviations from a stated coding-guideline expectation. lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed': the record was mined mechanically from source and no human review of the deviation has taken place. human_approval_status is 'pending' for the same reason. automated_review_status below refers to the corpus automation gates only and is not a statement about the engineering validity of the deviation.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Mined from the in-source Axivion MISRA C:2012 style-check suppression at commit 308028fb. Rationale text is verbatim from the source comment.

deviation_rationale: Function-like macro needed for this feature. Parenthesis stripping is intended here.
review_disposition_note: The Disable at line 248 names four check families in one annotation: 'MisraC2012Directive-4.9 MisraC2012-20.7 Generic-NoUnsafeMacro CertC-PRE01', but the matching Enable at line 255 names only three ('MisraC2012Directive-4.9 MisraC2012-20.7 Generic-NoUnsafeMacro') and drops CertC-PRE01. The suppression extent is therefore ambiguous: under the literal reading CertC-PRE01 remains enabled and the rationale claims to cover it. No waiver artifact was found. Governance evidence search at the pinned baseline: no deviance log, deviation log, suppression register, waiver file or review record for the MisraC2012 style checks exists anywhere in the repository (searched for *deviance*, *deviation*, *misra*, *axivion* file names and for 'AXIVION' across docs/). docs/tools/static-analysis/ and conf/spa/ do not exist at this commit. The rationale text below is therefore the only recorded justification.
reanalysis_justification: GEN_STRIP(x) expands to GEN_GET_ARGS x, which is a deliberate parenthesisation trick: it only works because a parenthesised argument is accepted as a single macro argument and then unwrapped. It therefore silently succeeds or fails based on how the caller wrote the argument, which no static analysis can fully check. Re-analyse on every new GEN_STRIP call site, on any change to the GEN_REPEAT_U family that consumes it, and whenever the tool's CertC-PRE01 support changes, since the Disable/Enable mismatch on that family leaves the intended extent undetermined.

design_traceability.coverage_note: general.h is in no implementation_mapping in the as_is profile. GEN_STRIP is the companion of GEN_REPEAT_Ux (FB2-SW-DEV-000020) and is used to strip parentheses from array-initialiser repetition counts. Recorded as a coverage gap.

impact_notes.note: The macro is documented as 'Strips a token of its surrounding parenthesis', which is by construction a construct that cannot be checked: correctness depends entirely on the caller's spelling of the argument.
The Disable annotation claims four check families and the Enable closes three, so the suppression extent for CertC-PRE01 is undetermined in the source itself.
Variadic macros plus argument-parenthesis elision; the technique is a preprocessor workaround, which is what the Directive-4.9 deviation records.
No as_is test artifact exercises GEN_STRIP directly; its behaviour is only reachable through the GEN_REPEAT_U family.

project_process_evidence.what_it_states: Project-level MUST: 'Code contributed to this project **MUST** be compatible with MISRA C:2012 which is described in :cite:`MISRA-C:2012`.' This is the only occurrence of 'MISRA' in the whole pinned docs/ tree and is the statement every suppression in this record set is a deviation from.

C:015 defines the project's only documented in-source deviation annotation syntax: 'If no assertion can be made for the parameter ... the parameter **MUST** be marked like this at the start of the function context: /* AXIVION Routine Generic-MissingParameterAssert: *ENTITY_NAME*: *RATIONALE* */.' The written guideline therefore mandates the '<ENTITY>: <RATIONALE>' annotation shape for one Axivion check family only; the MisraC2012 style-check family follows the same shape in practice but is not covered by any C:001..C:033 rule.

The project's own C coding guideline is a 33-rule set (C:001..C:033) with an 'Automated Check' column. Only C:002, C:004, C:005, C:006 and C:029 are marked 'Yes'; no rule in the set corresponds to a MisraC2012 style check, so the guideline set does not govern the rules these suppressions waive.

The third-party tool criticality table classifies git, TI ARM CGT, gcc, vs-code, waf, sphinx, ceedling and a custom HIL runner. No static-analysis tool (Axivion, cppcheck or equivalent) is classified, so no tool criticality or qualification basis for the tool that produced these suppressions is recorded in the repository.

corpus_scope.query: graft grep "AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012" -i (repo root)
corpus_scope.scope_note: This set is 26 deviation records, one per (file, symbol) group, and covers all 43 'AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012*' annotation lines found under src/ at commit 308028fb. Those 43 annotation lines fall in 20 files, and every one of the 43 is represented in the affected_lines of a record. 26 records cover 43 annotation lines over 26 distinct (file, symbol) groups because, where one symbol carries more than one MisraC2012 rule, the additional Disable lines appear as further entries in the same record's deviations array instead of as separate records. Axivion annotations outside this query are not mined by this set, and their absence must not be read as 'no deviation': 'AXIVION Routine Generic-MissingParameterAssert', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Style MisraC2012*', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-LocalInclude', 'AXIVION Next Codeline CodingStyle-Naming.*', 'AXIVION Next Codeline IISB-LiteralSuffixesCheck', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-NoEllipsis', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-ForbiddenFunctions', 'AXIVION Routine FaultDetection-DivisionByZero', and the 'AXIVION Routine MisraC2012Directive-4.1' / 'AXIVION Routine MisraC2012-2.7' annotations. Non-MISRA families that share one of the 43 mined annotation lines ARE recorded, per record, in tool_reference.co_located_non_misra_checks and in the corresponding deviations entry (for example Generic-NoUnsafeMacro, CertC-PRE01, Generic-NoEmptyLoops, Generic-DoxygenCommentInHeader, Generic-NoMagicNumbers, IISB-LiteralSuffixesCheck); out-of-query suppression sites on the same symbol are likewise listed in the record's deviations array with a note, so that each record's rule exposure is complete for the symbol it names.
